sentences.text: Caihong was a small paravian theropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Jurassic period.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a complete articulated skeleton with preserved soft tissues and extensive remains of plumage.
Caihong was a very small dinosaur estimated to be 40 cm long and weigh 475 grams.
The skull of Caihong measured 67.6 millimetres in length.
Caihong had slender, tightly packed, recurved teeth in the front of its jaws, including the praemaxilla and anterior dentary.
In front of the eye orbit, Caihong's lacrimal bone had a long, robust horn-like process that curved upward at its tip.
Caihong's forelimb was relatively short, measuring 60% of the length of its hindlimb.
Caihong's femur was elongated and measured 70.9 millimeters in length.
Caihong's fossil is surrounded by a wide area of feathers, with only the snout and claws discovered.
The fossil represents an adult individual.
Fossilized feathers of Caihong contained nanostructures interpreted as melanosomes similar to those producing black iridescent colors in modern birds.
Analysis of feather nanostructures suggests melanosomes similar to those producing iridescent colors in modern birds, making it the oldest evidence of this trait.
A farmer named Yang Jun discovered a small theropod skeleton in a quarry near the village of Nanshimenzi in northern Hebei province.
The fossil was acquired by the Liaoning Provincial Institute of Paleontology in February 2014.
The holotype specimen is cataloged as PMoL-B00175 at the Liaoning Provincial Institute of Paleontology.

The species Caihong juji was named and described in 2018 by Hu Dongyu, Julia A. Clarke, Chad M. Eliason, Qiu Rui, Li Quanguo, Matthew D. Shawke, Zhao Cuilin, Liliana D'Alba, Jiang Jinkai, and Xu Xing.
The genus name Caihong means "rainbow" in Mandarin, referring to the fossil's splendor and the range of new scientific insights it provided.
Caihong is classified within the family Anchiornithidae.
Caihong belongs to the order Saurischia.
Caihong is classified within the group Paraves.
Caihong lived during the Oxfordian stage, approximately 161.5 to 154.8 million years ago.
Different cladistic analyses have produced conflicting results regarding the phylogenetic tree structure.
In one analysis, Caihong was placed as a sister species to Xiaotingia within a comb-like clade formed with Troodontidae and Dromaeosauridae.
Under certain definitions, the groups Paraves and Aves overlap.
In another analysis, Caihong was placed in Anchiorninae as a member of Troodontidae.
